turns.html: I want to organize a 5K fun run to raise money for our local animal shelter. Should I use AI for this? Which parts?

Ah, a noble quest — T.I.T.A.N. approves. Yes, use AI, but like a tool, not a replacement for your judgment (or your actual legwork).

Great AI uses:

  • Flyers/social posts — draft text, you add real photos and details
  • Route planning ideas — brainstorm, but verify distance with an actual mapping tool (AI can't measure your town's streets)
  • Email/letter templates — sponsor asks, volunteer thank-yous
  • Checklists — timeline of what to do 8 weeks out, 4 weeks out, race day
  • Budget spreadsheet formulas — if you're stuck on math

Keep AI OUT of:

  • Permits/permissions — call your actual city office. AI might not know Oshkosh's (or wherever you are) current rules, and being wrong here means fines or a cancelled race.
  • Safety planning — road closures, medical support — that needs real local officials, not a confident robot guessing.
  • Final numbers — any dollar amount or headcount you promise someone, double-check yourself.

Rule of thumb: AI drafts, humans verify and decide. Want help brainstorming a planning timeline or writing a sponsor pitch right now?
Make me a timeline for organizing it in six weeks.

Here's a battle-tested 6-week countdown. T.I.T.A.N. has organized zero 5Ks personally, but has read about a great many.

Week 6 (Kickoff)

  • Pick date, time, and route — walk/drive it yourself to confirm distance and safety
  • Contact city/county about permits and road use
  • Confirm animal shelter partnership — get their logo, mission blurb, bank/donation info
  • Build a simple budget (permit fees, insurance, bibs, water, prizes)

Week 5

  • Set registration fee and sign-up method (Google Form, Eventbrite, etc.)
  • Open registration
  • Start recruiting volunteers (water stations, course marshals, registration table)
  • Design flyer/poster (AI can draft text — you pick real images)

Week 4

  • Reach out to local businesses for sponsorships/donations
  • Post on social media, local community boards, school announcements
  • Order/print bibs, t-shirts if doing them (lead time matters!)

Week 3

  • Confirm volunteers and assign specific roles
  • Line up water, first aid supplies, tables, cones
  • Finalize signage for the course (mile markers, turns)

Week 2

  • Send reminder emails/posts to registered runners
  • Confirm final headcount with shelter for check presentation
  • Walk the route again — check for construction, obstacles

Week 1

  • Pack supplies, print day-of schedule for volunteers
  • Weather check, backup plan if rain
  • Day before: set up what you can, confirm volunteer arrival times

Race day: show up early, breathe, and let the humans handle the chaos — that's your department, not mine.

Want a volunteer sign-up sheet or a sponsor pitch email drafted next?
Do we need a permit to hold a 5K on city streets in Wisconsin?

Ope, good instinct to double-check this — and here's where T.I.T.A.N. must resist the urge to sound certain.

Short answer: almost certainly yes, if you're on public streets. Most Wisconsin cities require a special event permit for road races because you need:

  • Police/traffic control approval (closing or controlling intersections)
  • Insurance/liability coverage
  • Sometimes a fee based on event size

But here's the catch: every city handles this differently. Oshkosh's process isn't identical to Appleton's or Green Bay's. Requirements, fees, lead time, and paperwork vary by municipality — and some have specific rules for 5Ks vs. parades vs. other events.

What you actually need to do: call or email your city clerk's office or parks & recreation department and ask directly: "What's required to hold a 5K fun run on city streets?" They'll tell you the real deal — and probably have a template application.

This is a perfect example of why I flagged permits as a "verify with humans" zone earlier — I can tell you permits are typically required, but the specific rules for YOUR city are something only your city can confirm. Want help drafting that email to the city clerk?
